text:
DISPATCH · Wed, Nov 11, 2026

01 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: one square mile of America, in code. In 1785 the young United States began dividing the land west of the Ohio River into sections one mile on a side, and the roads that followed still run a mile apart across the Midwest. SECTIONS, the first long form, fully onchain generative project by Grant Yun (@GrantYun2), takes that grid as its subject: farmland, centre pivot fields and grain elevators, then street grids, towers and freeways. Each work lists figures converted from US federal data for the land it shows, from residents to water use. It launches with Fellowship (@fellowshiptrust) on Nov 18: 1,300 sections as 1/1s on OpenSea (@opensea) and 12 Megacities in a 24-hour auction. NODE (@nodefnd) in Palo Alto opens a Sections exhibition on Nov 19.

02 · A museum as a city lab. In Shenzhen, the Guan Shanyue Art Museum has opened Gezhi Laboratory: Tech-Art and Future City, through Dec 11. It is the first show of a new Shenzhen City Art Lab, run with the China Academy of Art, after artists and writers spent three days this spring inside 12 research institutes, from genomics to AI and synthetic biology. Of 21 works, 13 were made by artists and scientists together, in four sections: landscape, city, future and generation. The landscape section uses AI to rewrite the brush and ink of the Lingnan school.

03 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: a painting that learned from Polaroids. In the early 1980s David Hockney built pictures from grids of Polaroids, each taken from a slightly different place and moment. Back on canvas in London in 1982, he painted David, Celia, Stephen and Ian on eight equal canvases, each sitter split at the waist so the seams do the work of the Polaroid borders. It comes to auction for the first time at Phillips (@phillipsauction) New York on Nov 17, estimated at $10 to 15 million.

04 · A palace turned into a camera. On Nov 13, Benrath Palace in Düsseldorf opens Upside Down // Inside Out by Bärbel Möllmann, through Dec 20, 2027. She sets three ways of making an image side by side: a walk-in camera obscura lit by the palace's own windows and garden, the photograph, and images generated by AI from language and data. The show treats them as parallel processes, not a line from old to new. Admission is free.

05 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: the machine, bound in tin. On Nov 27, 1968, MoMA (@MuseumModernArt) opened The Machine as Seen at the End of the Mechanical Age, more than 200 works chosen by Pontus Hultén of Moderna Museet (@ModernaMuseet), with a catalogue bound in tin can steel. From a Dürer woodcut and Duchamp to a Bugatti Royale, it also showed nine new works from an E.A.T. competition pairing artists with engineers, while all 150 entries went on view at the Brooklyn Museum (@brooklynmuseum). Kenneth Knowlton of Bell Labs (@BellLabs) presented an evening of computer-made film.

DISPATCH · Tue, Nov 10, 2026

01 · A painter made of code. Jake Eaton (@jkeatn), on staff at Anthropic (@AnthropicAI), shared paintings he has spent weeks making with Claude Fable 5.2, which Anthropic introduced yesterday. To answer the critique that earlier AI paintings only emulated real art, he asks the model to invent artist personas, each with a backstory and a style roughly identifiable in time. Every painting is a Python program, some one to two thousand lines long, that places each stroke through a simulated paint engine with different bristles. Most take a few thousand strokes. No image model is used, and nothing is rendered or traced in advance.

02 · Five years of HUMAN ONE. Last night Beeple (@beeple) marked five years since HUMAN ONE began. Christie's (@ChristiesInc) sold the kinetic sculpture on Nov 9, 2021 for $28.9 million: four video screens in an 87-inch polished aluminum case, paired with an NFT, both of which he can update remotely. Since then its explorer has moved through seven chapters, shown at Castello di Rivoli, M+, Crystal Bridges, the Deji Art Museum, the Mori Art Museum (@mori_art_museum) and NODE in Palo Alto. The latest, Pre-Human Feedback, asks how we shape the machines we train while they shape us.

03 · A mixtape for the museum. HEK Basel and the Tezos Foundation (@TezosFoundation) have named Tina Rivers Ryan (@TinaRiversRyan) curator of the second virtual exhibition in their 2026 partnership, per Art on Tezos (@artontezos_). Apocalyptic Wallpaper, Vol. 1 opens Dec 14 and works like a mixtape: artists who use digital tools to make audiovisual experiences, from generative music videos to live algorave performances and virtual nightclubs. A kiosk in the HEK lobby will show it on site as well as online, with accompanying NFTs on objkt (@objktcom) and a virtual opening tour with Ryan. Artists will be announced in coming weeks.

04 · Between the prompts in Lahore. The first VXR Festival, Pakistan's virtual and extended reality festival, opened Sunday to a full house at Alliance Française de Lahore, Dawn reports. Titled Between the Prompts // V.1 and curated by Dr Najamul Assar and Sarah Rajper, it brings together 70 artists from Pakistan, Spain, France, Canada, the United States and beyond, with support from the Institut français and in collaboration with UNESCO (@UNESCO). It continues in Lahore through Nov 12, then runs in Islamabad Nov 13 to 15.

05 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: a video lab anyone could use. In July 1971, Ralph Hocking opened the Experimental Television Center in Binghamton, New York, where anyone could borrow video gear. Within a year Nam June Paik and Shuya Abe were building a Paik/Abe Video Synthesizer on site, and one unit stayed so visiting artists could use it free of charge. In 1972 the Everson Museum of Art showed about 40 tapes from the Center. After a move to Owego in 1979, the residency hosted more than 1,500 artists, among them Gary Hill, Joan Jonas, Bill Viola and Barbara Hammer, until it closed in 2011. Its tapes and papers went to Cornell's (@Cornell) Rose Goldsen Archive.

DISPATCH · Mon, Nov 9, 2026

01 · Generative art did not begin with the computer. Interface Gallery (@Interface_art) and Lohaus Gallery (@LOHAUSGALLERY) have unveiled Harm van den Dorpel's (@harmvddorpel) Entfaltung for Zero 10: Generation at Art Basel Miami Beach (@ArtBasel), Dec 4 to 6: 36 unique generative works and 12 plotter drawings finished by hand. He starts from Emma Kunz's pendulum drawings, rebuilds her radial constructions in code, which he calls algorithmic archaeology, then lifts the points into space and sets them moving. The algorithm is stored entirely on Ethereum: three new blocks rotate each drawing, a fourth sets its next configuration. He treats the language model he worked with the way Kunz treated her pendulum. Collector Tristan Spits (@TristanSpits) has already added one to his collection.

02 · What photography after photography might become. Gallery byGRIDA (@bygrida) brings Memory Matter Media: The Korean Image from Photography to Digital Art to Paris Photo (@ParisPhotoFair), Nov 12 to 15 at the Grand Palais, in the digital sector. Nineteen artists, in partnership with Art on Tezos (@artontezos_), mark 140 years of Korea–France diplomatic relations. The show traces Korean image culture from traditional forms through war and division to AI, XR and generative imagery. An http://objkt.one (@objktone) release on Nov 11 features nakta (@nakta_j), Regina Kim (@reginagraphic), uttermelon (@uttermelon) and Yeonjeong Jang.

03 · A city as the screen. Dubai Culture (@DubaiCulture) has detailed the art programme of ISEA2026, the 31st International Symposium on Electronic/Emerging Art, running in Dubai through Nov 15 under the theme ELYAH: Constellating Place, Data and Identity. More than 100 showcases fill over 20 locations, the largest edition in the symposium's history, up to a nightly slot on the Burj Khalifa. And from today, Alserkal Avenue hosts The Window in Alserkal, a public digital art show from the CHANEL Culture Fund through Nov 29, including Farah Al Qasimi's video Signs of Life (2023), per her gallery The Third Line (@thethirdline).

04 · The museum writes back. Jenny Holzer has put words in public space for over 45 years, on posters, illuminated signs, projections and stone. For J'AI VU, made with and for the Musée d'Orsay's 40th anniversary, the museum supplies part of the text itself: fragments of its own documentation and writing from the period its collection covers. The brochure lists more than 750 texts from 424 sources and 73 authors. On view in Paris through Feb 21, 2027.

05 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: the corners before the code. Wassily Kandinsky's Betonte Ecken (1922–23), painted in Weimar early in his Bauhaus years, leads Christie's (@ChristiesInc) 20th Century Evening Sale in New York on Nov 17, estimated at $60 to 80 million. A guarantor has committed above the artist's £37.2 million record. The Guggenheim (@Guggenheim) sold it in 1964 for £22,000, about $62,000 then. Free public viewing at Rockefeller Center runs through Nov 17.

DISPATCH · Sat, Nov 7, 2026

01 · From a CRT line to an AI turtle. Yesterday MMCA (@MMCAKOREA) opened Nostalgia for Technology at Cheongju, through Mar 14, 2027: 26 works by 23 artists across more than 60 years of new media. Nam June Paik's Zen for TV (1963, remade 1995) turns a broken horizontal line upright into meditation. Ian Cheng's (@eyecheng) Thousand Lives (2023) is a real-time AI simulation whose virtual turtle searches for food, rests and responds to its surroundings. The collection show runs from electronic circuits and CRT TVs to generative art.

02 · A special cut of generative history, today. At 15:00–16:30 London GMT (10:00–11:30 Toronto EST), V&A South Kensington (@V_and_A) screens Ben Spilling's special cut of Generative, followed by a Q&A with the director, producer and digital art curator Melanie Lenz. Rare archive and interviews with Vera Molnar, Manfred Mohr and a new generation trace how code and chance entered the studio. The free screening accompanies Degrees of Disruption: Vera Molnar and Generative Art, on view through May 30, 2027.

03 · Measuring as a way of making worlds. Harvard FAS CAMLab (@HarvardCAMLab) opens Measuring the Cosmos: From Mandala to the Latent Space today, through Nov 21 in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The exhibition considers AI latent spaces as cosmograms alongside older ways of mapping the universe. Seven artists include Behnaz Farahi, Rohini Devasher and Yufeng Zhao, whose Earth is the Oldest Stereoscope pairs simultaneous views of the Moon from Boston and Santiago in dialogue with Paik. Today's opening is 14:00–18:00 Cambridge EST (the same in Toronto); regular hours are Fri–Sun, 11:00–16:00 EST. Free; registration required.

04 · Three final clocks after Bitcoin Amsterdam. Bitcoin Museum & Art Gallery (@BMAG_HQ) says its three remaining auctions close today, with scheduled hammers at 14:00, 14:30 and 15:00 Amsterdam CET (08:00, 08:30 and 09:00 Toronto EST). Late bids extend the clock. They follow BMAG's 20-work, six-artist presentation for the Nov 5–6 conference at SugarFactory in Halfweg. Fixed-price works are also listed in the online collection.

05 · Tonight, the network becomes the medium. Separately, Bitcoin Art Society (@BtcArtSociety) holds Art on Bitcoin: Public Show at What Is Happening Here Gallery, Amsterdam, 17:00–19:00 CET (11:00–13:00 Toronto EST). BitArt (@BitArt21) presents Mosaic, whose rules translate satoshi positions and UTXOs into an evolving visual and musical composition; the artist counts more than 127 million tiles. CyberSea (@CyberSeaNFT) presents Code Is Art, followed by a panel. Registration for the presentation evening is subject to approval.

DISPATCH · Fri, Nov 6, 2026

01 · Code becomes thread. Art Blocks (@artblocks_io) will bring Emily Xie's (@emilyxxie) Tensile Forms to Art Basel Miami Beach (@ArtBasel), Dec 2 to 6. An algorithm generates biomorphic forms; Xie collages computational textures and colors before translating them into embroidery. Large works are sewn by hand, smaller ones by machine. This morning the fair put Zero 10's second Miami edition in focus: Generation brings together 19 projects from 21 galleries and platforms.

02 · A city that reads the chain. Adam Weitsman (@AdamWeitsman) has acquired Dave Krugman's (@dave_krugman) CITY for $150,000, according to yesterday's sale report. Built with Transient Labs (@TransientLabs), the WINDOWS // NYC centerpiece is a dynamic 1/1 whose lights and relationships follow its onchain social graph. The acquisition also includes a large physical commission containing all 1,000 WINDOWS. Krugman says the related BUILDINGS mint closes in a week, on Nov 12.

03 · Ahead in Shanghai: an ocean made from forecasts. TANK Shanghai hosts a digital and AI art dialogue on Nov 12 alongside Terra Nova. Refik Anadol's (@refikanadol) Pacific Ocean B turns five years of Pacific wind-field forecast data into an immersive 4K AI painting. Pierre Huyghe's Camata has AI direct cameras and robotic arms around skeletal remains in the Atacama Desert, a film generated in real time. The exhibition runs through Jan 24.

04 · Three AI agents go out to take photographs. In Cezar Mocan's (@DrawingMoving) Arcadia Inc., agents walk a rendered pastoral and upload their pictures live. It joins Soft Signals at the Institut français in Cluj-Napoca (@InstitutFrancez), opening Nov 12 and on view Nov 13 to 22. Mélanie Courtinat's Indulto follows a torero toward a bull, then turns away when the fight begins. The six-artist show works with the gestures and pauses that become data, through simulation, sound and light.

05 · What survives when a digital work changes format? Yesterday's Verse (@verse_works) Talks brings Giannis Sourdis (@Greekdx) and Güerita Art (@GueritaArt) into a discussion of computer-art pioneers, artists' estates and collectors' responsibilities. Charles Csuri's (@CharlesCsuri) Ordo prompts the central question: where does preservation end and a change of medium begin? The 91-minute episode also takes up AI, scarcity, digital originals and physical prints.

DISPATCH · Thu, Nov 5, 2026

01 · Koyaanisqatsi becomes a room that watches you back. On Nov 21, Pérez Art Museum Miami (@pamm) and Onassis ONX open Techno Firma by John Fitzgerald and Godfrey Reggio, the museum's first artist-driven AI exhibition. A custom machine learning model trained on decades of Reggio's film negatives sets oceans and forests colliding with highways, factory lines and rocket launches across a monumental multi-screen obelisk. Computer vision reads the crowd: as visitors gather, the imagery speeds up and fractures, then collapses into darkness with Reggio's voice. It is the third iteration of The Vivid Unknown, first shown at BAM (@BAM_Brooklyn) in 2025.

02 · Forty years of letting nature paint. From Nov 7 to 22, Naoko Tosa (@Shintoism) shows Generative Beings in the Hall of Light at the Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art, free. It runs from An Expression (1985), in the collection of MoMA (@MuseumModernArt), to the new Tosa Rinpa: Spirit Resonance series, where sound, vibration, air, gravity and fluid motion make forms caught by high-speed cameras, then carried into moving image, gold-ground works, folding screens and glass. At a moment when "generation" means generative AI, the show offers a longer history.

03 · An AI that leads the workshop. Last night in Houston, Rashaad Newsome (@RashaadNewsome) brought Assembly, the documentary that follows his solo show at Park Avenue Armory (@ParkAveArmory), to The DeLUXE Theater for a screening. Its co-star is Being, the AI he built himself, first with GPT-Neo after a 2019 LACMA (@LACMA) Art + Technology Lab grant, then during a residency at Stanford (@Stanford), trained mainly on the writing of bell hooks, now including unpublished papers from the bell hooks Institute (@bellhooksinst). In the film Being narrates, answers its subjects and opens each session with a voguing lesson. "Rather than sitting on the side, I'm going to get in the game," Newsome says.

04 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: a last spring in Auvers. Painted in May 1890, weeks before Van Gogh died, Châtaigniers en fleurs has not been shown publicly since the Guggenheim (@Guggenheim) in 1964. On Nov 18 it leads Sotheby's (@Sothebys) 12-painting Blaquier-Arrieta evening sale in New York, estimated around $180 million, well above the artist's $117.2 million record. All 12 works are on view at 945 Madison Avenue from Nov 7, free with a timed reservation.

05 · And a history: in September 1970, visitors to Philips' (@Philips) Evoluon museum in Eindhoven met the Senster, Edward Ihnatowicz's 4 meter steel creature with a giraffe-like neck. Microphones and Doppler radar in its head let it lean toward quiet voices and recoil from shouts, run by a 16-bit computer with 8k of memory. It is considered the first robotic sculpture controlled by a digital computer. Dismantled in 1974, it stood outside a welding firm's office in Zeeland for over 40 years until AGH University of Krakow (@AGH_Krakow) revived it, and it returned for REBOOT at Nieuwe Instituut (@NieuweInstituut) in 2023.

DISPATCH · Wed, Nov 4, 2026

01 · A living world inside a cloud of silt. Sofia Crespo (@soficrespo91) and Feileacan McCormick, the duo behind Entangled Others (@entangledothers) and both keen divers, trained their own neural networks on footage from their dives to make Sediment Nodes (2022 to 2023), a generative video work in which murky water turns out to host algae, bacteria and small creatures that never existed. Minted on Ethereum and shown by the V&A (@V_and_A) and the Toledo Museum of Art (@ToledoMuseum), it comes to the East Slovak Gallery in Košice from Nov 9 to 30, part of EXTENDED, the gallery's platform for digital and new media art.

02 · Three chains, one museum. In Linz, the Francisco Carolinum (@ooeculture) is showing the collection it has built on the blockchain since 2021: more than 400 works by over 150 artists across Ethereum, Tezos and Bitcoin, from Larva Labs (@larvalabs) and Casey Reas (@REAS) to Rafaël Rozendaal (@newrafael) and LIA, curated by Julia Staudach, through Feb 7, 2027, with a twin presentation in Cryptovoxels. Among its latest additions is Beeple's (@beeple) EVERYDAYS: Late Stage Memetic Warfare, Day #6482. November brings an NFT workshop on the 13th, a catalogue launch for five years of the Digital Francisco Carolinum on the 19th and a livestreamed performance by Operator (@operator_______) on the 21st.

03 · Tell a phone your story and watch the walls change. On Nov 14 the Staten Island Museum (@SIMuseum) opens Anchoring Home by Stephanie Dinkins (@stephdink), an installation of video, sound and AI-generated imagery. Visitors speak into retrofitted telephones, and each voice flows through AI processes to reshape the images projected in the gallery, a generative document seeded with oral histories from the museum's collection, including the Black Angels of Sea View Hospital and residents of Sandy Ground. Dinkins was the inaugural winner of the LG Guggenheim Award (@Guggenheim) in 2023.

04 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: a head carved for a temple of beauty. Between 1911 and 1912 in Paris, Amedeo Modigliani cut Tête from a single block of limestone, one of a row of caryatids for a building he never made. Of his roughly 28 stone sculptures, most belong to museums, from MoMA (@MuseumModernArt) to Tate (@Tate). Never offered at auction and held in one collection for more than five decades, this one leads Phillips' (@phillipsauction) Modern & Contemporary Evening Sale in New York on Nov 17, estimated at $28 million to $35 million, the highest value sculpture Phillips has ever offered.

05 · And a history: in April 1965, Bell Labs (@BellLabs) researchers A. Michael Noll and Béla Julesz showed Computer Generated Pictures at the Howard Wise Gallery on West 57th Street, the earliest such show in the United States, two months after Georg Nees showed computer graphics in Stuttgart. The invitation was a small deck of IBM punch cards, visitors wore polarized glasses for the 3D works, and The New York Times (@nytimes) wrote that "the wave of the future crashes significantly at the Howard Wise Gallery." Not a single work sold.

DISPATCH · Tue, Nov 3, 2026

01 · Seven years of love letters to a CCTV manager end on Tezos. Since 2019 OONA (@madebyoona), an anonymous performance artist, has performed for the cameras of the London Underground and legally requested the footage, writing more than 400 emails to David, the Transport for London data manager who sends it. Dear David: A Surveillance Love Story, curated by Anika Meier, closed with a wedding at Shoreditch Arts Club during Frieze week, an empty space at the altar and a camera ring for a wedding ring. The Ceremony: OONA & David is now on objkt (@objktcom), and all 8 chapters live on Tezos. "They say love is blind. David sees everything."

02 · From Minecraft floors to hand-knotted wool. Travess Smalley's (@travess) Pixel Rugs began as Appalachian-style patterns he made to furnish his houses in Minecraft, then grew on Tezos from small grids and a few rules, layered until they tip toward order, chance or breakdown. On Nov 13, Galerie Met (@GalerieMet) in Berlin opens the project through Dec 5, curated by Kika Nicolela (@kikanicolela) with objkt: digital works, process animations, prints, woven rugs and a new monograph from Vetro Editions.

03 · Christie's (@ChristiesInc) held MAWASIM on Sunday, the first fine art auction in Abu Dhabi: 70 lots by 58 artists, $8,940,800 in total. After almost 7 minutes of bidding, Monir Shahroudy Farmanfarmaian's Variations on the Hexagon (2006) led at $844,800 against a $150,000 to $250,000 estimate, 1 of 6 mirror mosaic panels she made for the V&A's Jameel Gallery. "For me everything connects with the hexagon," she said.

04 · Ahead in Hong Kong: from Nov 5 to 15 the Hong Kong Arts Centre shows CONSENSUS, a solo exhibition by Liu Jiaying, CryptoZR (@CryptoZR_), curated by Gu Zhenqing. Fifteen works made with protocols, ledgers and code since 2017, including Red and Blue, 1000EYE and The Consensus, now in the Uli Sigg Collection, plus two new installations. In 2019 she introduced "Crypto Art" to China as 加密藝術, and in 2021 held what is billed as the world's first solo show of crypto art, in Beijing.

05 · Pasts that never happened. On Nov 14 Emi Kusano (@emikusano) opens End of Nostalgia, her largest solo show to date, at Hyper Museum Hanno in Saitama, through Jan 31, 2027. Built with generative AI, it turns the whole museum into one installation of new works, sculptures and prints, mining Japan's street cultures, from takenoko-zoku dancers to gyaru and decora, for scenes that feel remembered but never were.

06 · And a history: on March 17, 1960, Jean Tinguely's Homage to New York shook, burned and smoked itself apart in 27 minutes in the sculpture garden of MoMA (@MuseumModernArt). Built from bicycle wheels, a piano, a weather balloon and a bassinet, all painted white, it ran on a timer made by Billy Klüver of Bell Labs that closed 8 circuits every 3 minutes or so. The piano caught fire and the audience took the wreckage home. The E.A.T. archive counts it among the events that led to Experiments in Art and Technology.

DISPATCH · Mon, Nov 2, 2026

01 · Shanghai gives data art a festival of its own. On Friday the China Shanghai International Arts Festival opened the first show of X-TRA, its new visual art strand for digital work, at TANK Shanghai, the museum built inside former oil tanks, through Jan 24, 2027. Curated by the collector Qiao Zhibing, it brings together five artists and one duo on data and algorithms in art. Refik Anadol (@refikanadol) turns Pacific wind forecast data into flowing images, Pierre Huyghe's Camata lets AI edit footage shot in Chile's Atacama Desert in real time, Qiu Anxiong animates tales from the Tang dynasty in color ink, and Cao Shu draws on family memory through game engine imagery.

02 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: a hotel lit floor by floor. For the 8th ELEKTRA International Digital Art Biennial (@elektramontreal), its founder Alain Thibault has spread Lux Æterna through SonoLux, the Old Montréal hotel that bills itself as Québec's first contemporary art hotel. In the lobby, Matthew Biederman's Serial Mutations (z axis), a generative wall drawing driven by custom software and a projector, has run since 2014 without looping. Sabrina Ratté's Floralia (2021) sets flowers inside glowing, translucent virtual architecture, works by Baron Lanteigne and Inhwa Yeom fill the floors above, and a 20-minute sound work plays in the stairwells.

03 · A sentence you can only read in a mirror. On Saturday MMCA (@MMCAKOREA) opened its Museum Threshold Project in Cheongju with Rohwa Jeong, the duo of Noh Yunhui and Jeong Hyeonseok, through June 30, 2027. At the entrance, Passage sets embroidered panels at different angles in front of a mirror; walk around them and the marks on their backs join into one phrase, "How to Get to Tomorrow." On the building's media canvas, Still Life films the words "still life," embroidered in white on mosquito nets, at four places in Cheongju, from Sangdangsanseong Fortress to Chungbuk National University.

04 · In Tokyo, Kiyoshi Furukawa's retirement exhibition, Resonating Sound and Media, runs through Nov 8 at the University Art Museum of Tokyo University of the Arts, free. A composer and media artist who studied with Isang Yun in Berlin and György Ligeti in Hamburg, Furukawa wrote the virtual reality opera For Gods Yet Unborn for the opening of ZKM's new building in Karlsruhe in 1997, then came home in 2000 as the university's Department of Intermedia Art was being set up. The show mixes interactive works, research on sound, AI and care, and a concert.

05 · Ahead, two museums ask what AI does to art. On Nov 15, Museum Kranenburgh in Bergen, in the Netherlands, opens AI-Artist, through May 9, 2027: the critic and guest curator Edo Dijksterhuis gathers artists who use AI as a smart tool, artists who push back against it and artists who embrace it fully. On Nov 26 in Barcelona, Vectors: Art digital per pensar el futur, curated by Irma Vilà i Òdena, opens through Mar 14, 2027, from coexistence with machines and other species to the hidden infrastructure of the digital world, generative art and live creation.

DISPATCH · Sun, Nov 1, 2026

01 · A destructive agent, still in demand. XCOPY's (@XCOPYART) Breaker, a 2019 1/1 first minted on SuperRare (@SuperRare) with a single line of description, "Portrait of a destructive agent," joined a new collection on Friday in a private sale of $660,000. Eli Scheinman (@eli_schein), who facilitated the deal, called it "one of the truly great 2019 character pieces." The looping skull, boxed in cyan glitch and cut by bars of hot pink, sold for 200 ETH in 2021 and 100 ETH in 2024, as tracked by 24 Hours of Art (@24_Hours_Art). The new figure is the highest of the three in dollar terms, and the buyer has not been named.

02 · The web's invisible readers get a body. "Nowadays, much of the internet is explored not by humans, but by machines," opens the statement for Crawlers by Slava Rybin (@rybinfx), released on Ethereum by The Daily Program (@dailydotxyz) with OpenSea (@opensea). Its 1,111 creatures, built from points, squares and circles and moving like spiders and centipedes, each live on their own Wikipedia-style page, reading it, playing it as sound and writing new text beneath it with what Rybin calls "a boiled down LLM predictor." Saved as a bookmark, a crawler can be let loose on any website.

03 · In Lisbon on Saturday, Eterno Gallery (@EternoGallery) held ETERNO OPEN LAB, a free day on how digital art and AI change the way art is made and collected, from production to ownership. MAOTIK, the immersive and audiovisual artist Mathieu Le Sourd, spoke with Rudolfo Quintas and Camila Nogueira on installation and digital media, Mike Brauner gave a keynote on AI-led curation, and collectors talked first acquisitions, editions, display and preservation.

04 · A cautionary note from the market. Talis Protocol, an NFT marketplace built mainly on Injective, froze new listings and auctions after an attacker drained about 5,700 escrowed NFTs from its marketplace and auction contracts, reported Saturday. Dumped into standing collection offers, the haul came to roughly 445 INJ, about $3,100. Talis says it will return the stolen works, has begun returning more than 26,000 NFTs to their owners and plans to compensate bidders while a patched contract is reviewed.

05 · And a history: in 1976 Martha Wilson opened Franklin Furnace (@FranklinFurnace) in her Tribeca loft at 112 Franklin Street to show artists' books, and its basement became a stage for a generation of New York performance. Shut as an "illegal social club" in 1990 after a Karen Finley installation, it sold the loft in 1997 to "concentrate the program on broadcasting artists' ideas." In spring 1998, Franklin Furnace at Pseudo Programs, with Josh Harris's streaming network, gave 10 artists 50-minute netcasts, and the audience went from "75 people sitting on hard folding chairs" to viewers worldwide. Franklin Furnace turns 50 this year.

DISPATCH · Sat, Oct 31, 2026

01 · Orpheus among the kouroi. William Kentridge's Imitate the Sleep of Stones opened Friday at the Hellenic National Archaeological Museum in Athens, curated by Burcu Fikretoğlu, through Jan 24, 2027. Built on the myth of Orpheus going down to the underworld to bring Eurydice back, it places rust-painted steel figures and paper tree silhouettes among the museum's kouroi, sphinxes and funerary monuments. At its center is a diorama that uses Pepper's Ghost, the 19th-century theatre trick, to float reflected moving images inside a physical model. Kentridge's L'Orfeo is on stage at the Greek National Opera through Nov 14.

02 · New on http://catalogue.gallery: you can touch the grass. Leander Herzog's (@lennyjpg) Field is on view at Nguyen Wahed (@nguyenwahed) in New York through Nov 21, a field of grass computed live in JavaScript and WebGPU that never repeats a frame. It is split into 26 tokens on his own contract on Ethereum, one curated view per letter of the alphabet, and touching the grass in one view shows up in every view that sees that spot, in real time, with no wallet needed. "A screen with a static image is like a stuffed animal," he wrote. Mimi Nguyen (@drmiminguyen) put it simply: "Touch grass (literally)."

03 · Today in Taipei, the Taipei Digital Art Festival opens under the theme Gray Autonomous Entity, through Nov 15, with more than 30 Taiwanese and international teams, its main show set for the first time in the Taipei Expo Future Life Pavilion. Curated by Lien-Cheng Wang and Yen-Ju Lin, it treats AI as something living alongside plants, soil, fungi, animals and people. Jed Berk's Belugas' Sphere grows his 2008 Beluga Pod into a group of mechanical belugas that gather and move with the light and keep acting when no one is there.
